data.long_meaning: Sammad means protector or guardian. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'sammadah' which means to be firm or steadfast. It is also related to the Arabic word 'samidah' which means to endure or persist. Thus, the name Sammad reflects the idea of someone who is strong, powerful, and unyielding in their beliefs and actions.

historical_references.reference: Sammad ibn Qyays was a prominent leader of the Banu Asad tribe during the pre-Islamic period of Arabia. He is known for his role in the Battle of Buwat, which took place around 515 AD. The battle was fought between the Banu Asad and the Banu Hanifa tribes over control of the oasis of Buwat in the Najd region. Sammad was a skilled warrior and tactician, and his leadership played a crucial role in the victory of the Banu Asad.

Sammad ibn Mansur al-Khawlan was a prominent Sufi scholar and poet from the city of Khawlan in Yemen. He is known for his contributions to Sufi literature and philosophy, particularly in the areas of spiritual self-purification and the unity of God. He lived during the early Islamic period, around the 11th century AD, and his works continue to be studied and respected by Sufi scholars and practitioners today.
